verses.text: Jacob kept traveling and reached the land of the eastern peoples. 🧭
He spotted a field well with three flocks of sheep laid out beside it. They watered the flocks from that well, and a huge stone covered its mouth. 🐑
When all the flocks gathered, the shepherds rolled the huge stone away, watered the sheep, then put the stone back over the well. 💧
Jacob asked, “My relatives, where are you from?” They said, “We’re from Haran.” 🗣️
He asked, “Do you know Laban, son of Nahor?” They said, “Yes, we know him.” 👀
He asked, “Is he doing well?” They said, “He’s doing well. Look, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.” 🐑
Jacob said, “It’s still the middle of the day—nowhere near time to gather the livestock. Give the sheep water, then take them back to graze.” ☀️
They said, “We can’t until all the flocks gather and someone rolls the stone from the well. Then we’ll water the sheep.” 🐑
While Jacob was still talking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep—she was the one tending them. 🐑
When Jacob saw Rachel, daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, and Laban’s sheep, he went over, rolled the stone away, and watered his uncle’s flock. 💪
Jacob kissed Rachel, raised his voice, and burst into tears. 😭
Jacob told Rachel, “I’m your father’s relative—and Rebekah’s son.” She ran and told her father. 🏃
When Laban heard his sister’s son Jacob had arrived, he ran to meet him, hugged him, kissed him, and brought him home. Jacob told him the whole story. 🤗
Laban said, “You really are my own flesh and blood.” Jacob stayed with him for a month. 🏠
Laban asked Jacob, “Just because you’re my relative, should you work for free? Tell me—what should I pay you?” 💬
Laban had two daughters: Leah, the older one, and Rachel, the younger. 👭
Leah’s eyes were weak, while Rachel had a beautiful form and was attractive. 👀
Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, “I’ll work for you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.” ❤️
Laban said, “Better I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me.” 🤝
Jacob worked seven years for Rachel. The time flew by like a few days because he loved her. ⏳
Jacob told Laban, “Give me my wife. My time is up; I want to go in to her.” 💬
Laban gathered all the men of the place and threw a feast. 🎉
That evening, Laban brought his daughter Leah to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her. 🌙
Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a servant. 👩‍👧
Morning came—and plot twist, it was Leah! Jacob confronted Laban: “What have you done to me? I worked for Rachel! Why did you deceive me?” 😳
Laban said, “That’s not how we do things here: the younger daughter doesn’t marry before the firstborn.” 📜
Finish Leah’s wedding week, and I’ll give you Rachel too, in exchange for another seven years of work.” ⏳
Jacob did that and completed Leah’s wedding week. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as a wife. 💍
Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as a servant. 👩‍👧
Jacob went in to Rachel too. He loved Rachel more than Leah, and worked for Laban another seven years. ❤️
Yahweh saw that Leah was unloved, so He opened her womb. Rachel, though, was unable to conceive. 🙏
Leah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, saying, “Yahweh has seen my suffering. Maybe now my husband will love me.” 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to another son. “Yahweh heard that I’m unloved and gave me this son too,” she said, naming him Simeon. 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to a son. “This time my husband will be joined to me—I’ve borne him three sons,” she said. So he was named Levi. 👶
She conceived again and gave birth to a son. “This time I’ll praise Yahweh,” she said, and named him Judah. Then she stopped giving birth. 🙏
